newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan voices fears over India missile report.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan voices fears over India missile report.

text.p: Pakistan voiced concern on Tuesday at a U.S. newspaper report that India had moved medium-range ballistic missiles to a prospective launch site near the border and said the move could trigger a regional arms race.
The Foreign Ministry, commenting on the Washington Post report in Tuesday's editions, said Pakistan "reserves the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its security".
"Pakistan is seriously concerned about the deployment by India of medium-range ballistic missiles...," a ministry statement said.
"The deployment of Prithvi missiles entails a qualitative change in the security environment in South Asia and could trigger a dangerous ballistic arms race in the region," the statement said.
In New Delhi, an Indian Defence Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday the ministry had "no information" on the report. He declined to elaborate.

Quoting U.S. officials, the Washington Post said India's actions had raised fresh concerns that the two foes, which have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947, had entered a provocative phase in their longstanding arms race.
The Prithvis are capable of carrying conventional but not nuclear warheads.

The officials told the newspaper that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that fewer than a dozen of the missiles were now located near the city of Jullundur in the state of Punjab in northwest India.
Some intelligence officials described the movement of the missiles as the first operational deployment of the Prithvi since its development began over a decade ago.
Other officials said it was unclear if all the equipment needed to launch the missiles had also been moved to the northwest border.
